posts.name: NinjaMonkey
posts.cooked:
After reading through this weeks update I was particularly concerned with the comment about "Characters are going to be incapped a lot in this game"(or something like that). When the character is incapped, you just choose another one and start again.

This concerns me for 2 reasons:

1. Even if you get to choose a new hero and just join the fight again, this feels like the equivalent of Citizen Dawn dropping THAT CARD over and over again. Meaning, for me, not fun at all. Constantly loosing all of your setup does not equal fun for me.

2. I don't mind having a hero incapped. It happens. What concerns me is the slow build heroes like Absolute Zero, Argent Adept, Bunker, Unity, etc. Is there ever going to be any point in playing these heroes in the Oblivaeon event if Heroes are just being incapped left and right, and losing all their setup in the process? Its looking like the slow build heroes are going to be relegated to the back of the box for this event.

I'm looking forward to the new heroes and environments. However, the more I read about the Oblivaeon event and play style itself, the less interested I'm getting in actually playing it. I'm hoping I'm wrong, and the new play style actually breathes new life into a game which for me has begun to grow a bit stale. I didn't particularly care for the vengeance play style so maybe that is coloring my feelings on this, as yet, unplayed play style.

posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
I'm not sure it's going to be "left and right." From the sound of it, there'll be some unlucky draws where maybe one hero goes down round one (A string of "Hits the hero with the lowest HP" cards, for instance). But that's possible in the game already -- you could easily lose all the Sentinels in Iron Legacy's first turn, for instance.

It's going to be rough, but I would be extremely disappointed if it was the normal case for heroes to not be able to make some contribution before they go down.

I highly doubt that this is going to be a problem.  While some villians are less fun for setup heavy heroes, OblivAeon is the big finale villain - they're going to be designing it with the intent of being fun to play using all heroes.

 

OblivAeon has gone through a metric ton of playtesting, and each hero is the personal favorite of some player.  If there's any hero for whom OblivAeon was specifically unfun to fight with, that would have been fixed long since.

 

Also, it looks to me like a great many of the Mission rewards grant extra plays and draws to the heroes, which should make setup even easier than before.  It's a lot less frustrating to lose a fully setup AZ if you can plop down AA with 3 instruments and 3 songs the next turn.  (I'm probably exaggerating, but you get my meaning)

posts.name: dprcooke
posts.cooked:
Plus, this actually brings a whole new area of strategy into the games that I can’t wait to try: when to bring a specific hero into the fight.
I mean, bringing Haka in early to eat Aeon Men all day for a super powerful Savage Mana would be great, but it’s not going to help much while OblivAeon has his 10k HP shield, and the longer Haka’s around the more likely he is to die. But bring him in too late and you won’t get the satisfaction of crushing Obliv with it.
So learning when the best time to bring specific Heroes into the fight (including those like Bunker and AZ) is going to be hugely fun for me.

posts.cooked:
I love the idea that if The temple of Zhu Long gets destroyed, a Ninja in a different Battle Zone will get removed from the game. 

 
 
Tempest was using everything he had to fend off waves of Aeon men within the winding hallways the Court of Blood, when a massive earthquake struck, shaking the ornate walls with such ferocity, that the heroes and vampires stopped fighting. Tempest turned around and saw a Zhu Long warrior let out a bloodcurdling scream, a noise that not even the Countess has heard in her lifetime. The screaming only ceased when he was torn out of existence, every part of him shredded into nothingness. Then there was nothing. The world stopped shaking, and the only noises the inhabitants could hear were the distant footsteps of Aeon men, and the blood dripping from the walls.  The Harpy collapsed to her knees, and shuddered. "They…they… didn't make it." As the footsteps grew louder, the heroes knew they couldn't stop. They needed to save everyone. They needed to save everything.
